claim.summary: Over F2[z,y], let E=(z+y)(z+y+1), C=y(y+1), B=z(z+1). For every M=2^t,t>=1, the three binary affine products E^(M+1), C^(M+1), B C^M sum to B^M E. Their common gcd and largest common Frobenius power in full-factor multiplicities are both1, while the sum has exact root order M at both0,1. Thus primitive triple contact is unbounded in a polynomial-size description and global common-power deflation followed by a fixed number of elementary root divisions does not suffice. The quotient is the cheap product E, obtained by regrouping C^(M+1)+B C^M=C^M E and applying Frobenius. H=E(F dot Z)^M for a nonempty unit class containing B has this as an actual reciprocal dividend. The control limits that tactic, not arbitrary regrouping, exact division or Frege proofs.

Its exact root order at both0,1 is M and its quotient s^M has depth at most two and size O(M+1) with ordinary power wires. Leading and constant coefficients rule out splitting of the base pair sums; translation handles the last pair and UFD preserves nonsplitting under powers. For any unit-generating binary input tuple F containing B with these distinct old variables, supply H=(s sum_(i!=B)Fi Zi)^M+Z_B^M sum_i Pi^M. It equals s^M(F dot Z)^M and is invariant on every full coefficient certificate. Its reciprocal numerator construction produces the literal triple after pruning the zero branch. Inputs of joint size u, depth delta_F and r labels give probe size O(u+r+M+1) and constant added depth. Polynomial M in a Boolean-unsatisfiable CNF encoding N gives unbounded polynomial-size source-admissible witnesses without a small certificate assumption. This refutes a mandatory affine-pair-merger step, not general division: complete factorization and global Frobenius deflation give cheap alternatives.
